docs.text: DAL_PDU software design Purpose DAL_PDU is the power distribution unit board of the IGRVT-50 PC104 stack. The current ATmega128A firmware controls a TRANS eFuse, heartbeat LED, and TPS55287 variable output; it offers text commands on UART0 and the software console, plus a Modbus RTU register subset on USART1. The broader design calls for power telemetry, fault logging, and a dual-bank bootloader; those features are not yet implemented. Start with Current firmware architecture for implemented modules and runtime flow, and Current command reference for commands available today. The requirements and use-case pages also describe planned features. Source hardware evidence All hardware facts in this documentation set are drawn from the independent hardware review at: D:\PROJECT\LIINSPACE\DAL\REVIEW\review_dal_pdu_docs\docs which covers SpaceLiinTech_BEE_DAL_PDU_HW_V1.0 (schematic PDF revision 1.1.0, dated 15-Sep-2026; BOM DAL_PDU_V1.0.xlsx ). That review's own conclusion is "Not ready for fabrication or assembly" — three blocking issues and several major issues are still open. See Hardware overview for the subset that directly constrains this software design, and treat the full issue register in the review package as the authority for hardware release status. The console is the software UART on PE3/PE4 ( MCU-001 , decided); see Hardware overview . The ATmega128A has exactly two hardware USARTs ( USART0 on PE0/PE1, USART1 on PD2/PD3). All three required serial channels (PC104 RS-232, local console, RS-485/Modbus) must be allocated across those two USARTs plus one software (bit-banged) UART — see Serial resource allocation . The implemented Modbus map and ASCII commands are described on the current-firmware pages. Additional registers and commands in the requirements remain design targets.

Code architecture This page describes how the current DAL_PDU firmware is layered, how data moves between modules, and which tasks own which state. It describes the code under PDU/firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/ . For the short overview see Current firmware architecture ; for the scheduler internals see Scheduler design . 1. Layers The source tree is organised in six numbered layers. Lower numbers are closer to the application; the M prefix is only a directory convention, not a build boundary. This is acceptable for maintenance commands but not for future user-facing commands. Duplicate overview. Current firmware architecture and this page cover the same layers. Layer inversion: resolved. bsp_tps55287.c owns its record, so M2 no longer calls into M1. The record is read through BSP_TPS55287_GetStatus() . The other records are still written by M0 modules, which is the expected direction. Command and BSP coupling. Command handlers call BSP directly, so the command tests need the BSP mocked. This is acceptable for maintenance commands but not for future user-facing commands. Duplicate overview. Current firmware architecture and this page cover the same layers. Keep the overview short and point it here for detail.

docs.text: Current text command reference The same case-sensitive commands run on UART0 and the software UART console at 9600 baud. Terminate a line with CR, LF, or CRLF; arguments are separated by spaces. Both ports echo input, begin with a > prompt, and send the reply to the port that received the command. The tables show reply text only , without echo or prompt. General and application commands Command example Expected reply Notes help Starts with Available commands and ------------------ , followed by all command help lines Entries are sent as the 256-byte response buffer drains. version DAL_PDU firmware v0.1.0 (Development) build c7f0bf8-dirty Firmware version and build. The build is the short git commit. -dirty means the tree had uncommitted changes when it was built. led get LED on=1000 ms off=1000 ms Default after reset. led set 250 750 LED on=250 ms off=750 ms Both decimal durations must be nonzero, at most 4294967295 ms. trans get TRANS off Adds fault if either eFuse fault input is active. trans on TRANS on If a fault is latched, the reply is TRANS fault and PC2 stays disabled. A live-but-not-yet-latched fault does not refuse this reply by itself (decided 2026-10-15, see Mode state machine §4 ); the 6 ms poll still catches it, latches it, and disables PC2 within one cycle regardless. trans off TRANS off Requests TPS55287 VOUT off before disabling TRANS. With an active fault, reply is TRANS off fault . I2C maintenance commands Addresses are 7-bit ( 0x08 – 0x77 ); register and data bytes are 0x00 – 0xff . Numbers accept decimal or a 0x hexadecimal prefix. The examples below assume one responding TPS55287 at address 0x75 and its reset register values. Command example Expected reply Notes i2cdetect 0x74 0x75 0x75 Scan inclusive range; the trailing space precedes CRLF. With no devices, the reply is an empty line. Plain i2cdetect scans 0x08 – 0x77 . i2cget 0x75 0x04 0x03 Reads one register byte using a repeated START. Without a register, reads one byte directly. i2cset 0x75 0x04 0x03 I2C write OK Writes one register byte. This example preserves the TPS55287 reset feedback setting; raw writes can change power configuration. An unresponsive address returns I2C error for i2cget or i2cset . 24C04 EEPROM commands U14 has 512 bytes at logical addresses 0 through 511 . Numbers accept decimal or 0x hexadecimal notation. The examples assume a connected chip and successful I2C transfers. Command example Expected reply Notes eeprom probe EEPROM present Reports EEPROM unavailable if the chip does not acknowledge. eeprom read 0x100 4 EEPROM 0x0100: de ad be ef Example assumes those four bytes were stored. Omitting the length reads one byte; length must be 1–16. eeprom write 0x100 deadbeef EEPROM write OK Writes four bytes and verifies them by reading back. The hex string must have 2–32 digits (1–16 bytes); an optional 0x prefix is accepted. Writes lower the PA0 write-protect pin only during the operation. The reply is EEPROM read failed or EEPROM write failed if the I2C transfer or verification fails. Out-of-range addresses, reads or writes past byte 511 , and malformed hex data return Invalid argument . TPS55287 output commands U5 is detected at 0x74 or 0x75 according to its MODE pin. The examples assume 0x75 and no active faults. tps55287 set and tps55287 on power TRANS on first if it is off, and confirm the chip answers, instead of requiring a separate trans on beforehand. tps55287 off never powers TRANS on just to turn itself off. This board wires an external feedback divider (R22 = 102 kΩ, R30 = 11.3 kΩ to GND; ratio ≈ 0.0997), not the chip's internal ratio. The TPS55287 resets to internal feedback (register 0x04 = 0x03 ) every time its EN /UVLO drops — including every time TRANS is power-cycled, since TRANS is off whenever VOUT is idle. So every successful TRANS power-up ( trans on , tps55287 set / on , or the equivalent Modbus write) also writes register 0x04 to 0x80 (external feedback) and reads it back to confirm. Every setpoint write and output-enable request checks that configuration again. If a raw I2C command changed it while VOUT was on, firmware disables VOUT before correcting feedback and re-enables it only after a successful setpoint write. tps55287 status 's internal-feedback / external-feedback text reflects whichever the chip is actually reporting at that moment. Command example Expected reply Notes tps55287 status TPS55287 addr=0x75 off external-feedback Appends SCP , OCP , or OVP for set protection flags. Reading status clears those latched flags. Does not power TRANS on; fails if TRANS is off. tps55287 set 5000 TPS55287 set OK Powers TRANS on first if it is off (which also re-asserts external feedback). Sets a nominal 5000 mV request against the external ratio. The actual output has not been measured by this command. tps55287 get VOUT setpoint 5002 mV Converted back from the stored reference code using whichever feedback mode and ratio the chip currently reports; register conversion may differ slightly from the requested millivolts. Does not power TRANS on; fails if TRANS is off. tps55287 on TPS55287 on Powers TRANS on first if it is off. Refused if a PC4/PC0 fault is latched, TRANS ends up off, the chip does not respond, or external feedback cannot be re-asserted. A live-but-not-yet-latched fault does not refuse this by itself; the 6 ms poll still catches and latches it shortly after. tps55287 off TPS55287 off Clears the chip's output-enable bit. Never powers TRANS on. tps55287 set and tps55287 on report TPS55287 set failed (TRANS) / TPS55287 enable failed (TRANS) if TRANS was off and powering it on failed (fault active, latched, the regulator did not respond, or external feedback could not be re-asserted — see Mode state machine ). With TRANS already on, tps55287 set rejects values below 800 mV and above ~12 V (the external ratio's range), reporting TPS55287 set failed (I2C or range) for an I2C failure or an out-of-range request. tps55287 on reports TPS55287 enable failed (I2C or TRANS interlock) if TRANS is faulted or I2C fails after TRANS is already on. A failed get or status reports TPS55287 read failed (I2C) . PAC1934 rail monitor The one-second background task reads U10 through the shared I2C bus. The board uses 10 mΩ shunts on all four channels. The example below assumes the device was detected at 0x1f and all channels measure 5 V, 1 A, and 5 W. Command example Expected reply Notes pac1934 get PAC1934 addr=0x1f followed by VOUT 5000 mV 1000 mA 5000 mW , +12 ... , +5_TRANS ... , and +5 ... Shows the latest cached sample; plain pac1934 and pac1934 status are aliases. pac1934 refresh Same format as get Takes a new measurement immediately; normal polling remains every 1000 ms. Before the first successful poll, or after a failed I2C read, the reply is PAC1934 unavailable . Rail labels follow channel order 1–4 in the board design; confirm the physical wiring and installed 10 mΩ shunts during bring-up; the hardware review found a shunt-value mismatch in the BOM. Board temperature The one-second temperature task samples the TC1047A on the TEMP net (PF1/ADC1), averaging 16 conversions. The reply is in degrees Celsius with one decimal place. Command example Expected reply Notes temp TEMP 25.1 C Shows the latest cached sample. temp get is an alias. temp refresh TEMP -0.2 C Takes a new sample immediately; normal sampling remains every 1000 ms. If the ADC fails or the reading is outside the TC1047A range of −40 °C to +125 °C, the reply is TEMP unavailable . The same value is available over Modbus as input register 30021 . Operating mode The mode is NORMAL, MANUAL, WARNING, or ERROR. See Mode state machine . Command example Expected reply Notes mode MODE normal and CAUSES regulator=0 pac1934=0 eeprom=0 latch=0 limit=0 setpoint=0 bus=0 link=0 mode get is the same. A 1 in CAUSES means that cause is active. link is Modbus link loss (no valid request for the configured timeout, default 5 s); it only raises WARNING and does not turn TRANS/VOUT off by itself. mode manual MODE manual Takes operator control even when an ERROR cause is set. A confirmed eFuse fault remains latched and reported, but software does not turn VOUT or TRANS off in MANUAL. mode normal MODE normal Checks the regulator and limits if either has raised ERROR, clears healthy causes, then leaves MANUAL. Refused with MODE refused: error while a cause remains or an eFuse fault is latched. Fault latch A fault that switches TRANS off is latched in the ATmega128A internal EEPROM, so it survives a reset. While any bit is latched, trans on is refused and VOUT cannot be enabled. The same latch is available over Modbus coil 00003 . Command example Expected reply Notes fault get FAULT latch pc4=0 pc0=0 active pc4=0 pc0=0 latch shows the stored bits. active shows the live eFuse inputs. pc4 is the 12V TRANS fault and pc0 is the 12V_MCU fault. Each is latched, and clears only when its input is inactive. fault clear FAULT latch cleared Clears the latch only. Refused with FAULT clear refused: fault still active while a fault input is active. TRANS stays off, and can be enabled again only when no fault input is active. A damaged EEPROM record is treated as both faults latched, so the unit stays off until the latch is cleared. Limits and events Over-temperature and overcurrent are checked every second in every mode. In NORMAL, a trip turns VOUT and TRANS off and sets the limit ERROR. In every mode, each trip is logged once as a WARNING event in the 24C04. mode normal clears the limit ERROR once the regulator responds and limits are back in range. The ERROR is stored in internal EEPROM, so it survives a reset until that check succeeds. Command example Expected reply Notes limit LIMIT temp=850 vout=1000 trans=1000 limit get is the same. Temperature is in tenths of a degree C, so 850 is 85.0 C. Currents are in mA. limit temp 900 LIMIT temp=900 vout=1000 trans=1000 Range -400 to 1250. Stored in internal EEPROM and used at the next check. limit vout 3500 LIMIT temp=900 vout=3500 trans=1000 Range 100 to 5000 mA. limit trans sets the +5_TRANS limit the same way. limit vout 70000 LIMIT refused: out of range Nothing changes. event get EVENT seq=1 sev=WARNING code=TEMP mode=NORMAL value=900 time=unset source=UNSET Lists the 24C04 ring, 32 slots. Codes are TEMP, VOUT_CURRENT, TRANS_CURRENT, CONFIG_CHANGED, SETPOINT_MISMATCH, and CLOCK_SET. Value is tenths of a degree C, mA, or mV, as the code says. time is UTC ( YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ ), or unset . source is where that time came from: UNSET , RESTORED , or SET . EVENT none when empty. Configuration The Modbus slave address and baud rate are read at boot. Modbus 40105 and 40106 show the active values. The communications timeout takes effect at once. Each change is logged once as an INFO event ( CONFIG_CHANGED ). Command example Expected reply Notes config CONFIG address=1 baud=9600 timeout=5 source=DEFAULT config get is the same. source=DEFAULT means no valid record is stored, so the compiled defaults are in use. source=EEPROM means the stored record is in use. config set address 7 CONFIG address=7 baud=9600 timeout=5 source=EEPROM , then Address and baud take effect after reboot Range 1 to 247. Takes effect at the next boot. config set baud 19200 CONFIG address=7 baud=19200 timeout=5 source=EEPROM , then the reboot line Supported: 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600, 19200, 38400. Takes effect at the next boot. config set timeout 10 CONFIG address=7 baud=19200 timeout=10 source=EEPROM Range 1 to 60 s, default 5. Outputs turn off after this long without a valid Modbus request. Takes effect at once. config set address 0 CONFIG refused: out of range Nothing changes. config set baud 115200 CONFIG refused: unsupported baud Nothing changes. config_reset confirm CONFIG reset to defaults , the CONFIG line, LIMIT temp=850 vout=1000 trans=1000 Restores the configuration and the limits to the defaults and stores them. The reboot line appears only if the address or baud changed. config_reset Invalid argument reply Without confirm nothing changes. config_reset does not clear the event log, the boot history, the fault latch, or a limit ERROR. A healthy mode normal request clears a limit ERROR. Input errors The console prints Unknown command , Too few arguments , Too many arguments , or Invalid argument for parser/handler errors. For example, led set 0 500 returns Invalid argument . Input lines longer than 63 characters return Line too long . A command response that fills the shared output buffer ends with [output truncated] . The larger proposed command set and power/telemetry requirements remain in Use cases, user stories & commands . The currently implemented Modbus register map is separate from these text commands. Telemetry Command example Expected reply Notes telemetry SETPOINT 5000 mV , then one line per rail SETPOINT unset until a setpoint is commanded since reset. Each rail line is VOUT , +12 , +5_TRANS , or +5 with measured mV, mA, and mW. PAC1934 unavailable when the monitor cannot be read. Setpoint setpoint get reports the commanded VOUT setpoint held in system data. It is the value last set by the console or by Modbus 40001 , and it does not read the chip. tps55287 get still reads the TPS55287 register. Command example Expected reply Notes setpoint get SETPOINT 5000 mV SETPOINT unset until a setpoint is commanded since reset. Boot information Each boot adds one to the boot count, which is kept in internal EEPROM. The cause comes from the reset flags read at startup. A watchdog fault is recorded before the TPL5010 resets the unit, and it is written to the boot record at the next boot. Command example Expected reply Notes bootinfo BOOT count=2 cause=CLIENT_WATCHDOG source=MODBUS bootinfo get is the same. Causes are POWER_ON, BROWN_OUT, EXTERNAL, AVR_WATCHDOG, CLIENT_WATCHDOG, COMMAND (from reset confirm ), and UNKNOWN. Sources are CONSOLE, HEARTBEAT, MODBUS, POWER_MONITOR, TEMPERATURE, and MONITOR. source=- unless the cause is CLIENT_WATCHDOG. bootinfo history lists the last 10 boots, newest first, from internal EEPROM. The same boot count, cause, and source are on Modbus input registers 30032 – 30034 . Clock A software clock keeps UTC from the last set and the scheduler tick. It has no battery. Every 15 minutes, and on each set, it stores a checkpoint in internal EEPROM. After a reset it restores the last checkpoint with source RESTORED , which is approximate, since the power-off time is unknown. A set from the console or Modbus gives source SET . Without a checkpoint the clock is UNSET . Events carry the clock time and its source. Command example Expected reply Notes time TIME 2026-10-06T12:34:56Z source=SET or TIME unset source=UNSET time get is the same. UTC. The source is UNSET , RESTORED , or SET . time set 1791290096 TIME 2026-10-06T12:34:56Z source=SET Sets the clock from Unix seconds. Logged as a CLOCK_SET event. time set 4294967295 TIME refused: reserved value The value means unset. Nothing changes. time set 17x Invalid argument reply Nothing changes. The clock uses the MCU clock. It has no temperature compensation, so it drifts with the crystal. The OBC should set it periodically. Modbus reads and sets the same clock: 40040 – 40041 to set and read, and 30039 – 30040 to read. Status and reset Command example Expected reply Notes status STATUS , then the replies of mode , temp , telemetry , fault get , and bootinfo , one after another Read-only summary for the technician. Each section has the same format as its own command. reset confirm RESET outputs off, restarting Turns VOUT and TRANS off, sends the reply, then restarts the MCU through the watchdog after about 0.1 s. The next boot reports cause=COMMAND . Without confirm nothing happens. reset Invalid argument reply Needs confirm . persist_reset internal confirm PERSIST_RESET internal EEPROM erased, restarting Turns VOUT and TRANS off, blanks every byte of internal EEPROM (fault latch, limit error, limit values, boot record and history, config, clock checkpoint), then restarts the same way reset confirm does, since all of that is cached in RAM at boot and needs a fresh init to pick up the now-blank EEPROM. Blanking takes under a second on a lightly-used chip (it skips bytes that already read 0xFF), well inside the TPL5010's 10 s window. persist_reset external confirm PERSIST_RESET external EEPROM erased Blanks the whole U14 24C04 (the event log ring). Nothing is cached from it at boot, so this does not restart the MCU or touch the outputs. A failed erase (chip not acknowledging) replies PERSIST_RESET external EEPROM failed . persist_reset internal , persist_reset external , persist_reset Invalid or too-few-arguments reply Each needs its scope ( internal or external ) and confirm . persist_reset is the only command that returns EEPROM to the state of a never-written chip; fault clear , mode normal , and config_reset confirm each clear a narrower, specific piece of internal EEPROM state (see Mode state machine §8 and the configuration section above). Design command names The firmware names are the reference. The design names below are dropped (OI-13). Design name Use instead STAT status FAULT? fault get FAULT CLR fault clear LOG? event get TEMP? temp get ILIM limit , limit vout , limit trans RESET reset confirm

docs.text: Each boot adds one to the boot count, which is kept in internal EEPROM. The cause comes from the reset flags read at startup. A watchdog fault is recorded before the TPL5010 resets the unit, and it is written to the boot record at the next boot. Command example Expected reply Notes bootinfo BOOT count=2 cause=CLIENT_WATCHDOG source=MODBUS bootinfo get is the same. Causes are POWER_ON, BROWN_OUT, EXTERNAL, AVR_WATCHDOG, CLIENT_WATCHDOG, COMMAND (from reset confirm ), and UNKNOWN. Sources are CONSOLE, HEARTBEAT, MODBUS, POWER_MONITOR, TEMPERATURE, and MONITOR. source=- unless the cause is CLIENT_WATCHDOG. bootinfo history lists the last 10 boots, newest first, from internal EEPROM. The same boot count, cause, and source are on Modbus input registers 30032 – 30034 .

docs.text: A software clock keeps UTC from the last set and the scheduler tick. It has no battery. Every 15 minutes, and on each set, it stores a checkpoint in internal EEPROM. After a reset it restores the last checkpoint with source RESTORED , which is approximate, since the power-off time is unknown. A set from the console or Modbus gives source SET . Without a checkpoint the clock is UNSET . Events carry the clock time and its source. Command example Expected reply Notes time TIME 2026-10-06T12:34:56Z source=SET or TIME unset source=UNSET time get is the same. UTC. The source is UNSET , RESTORED , or SET . time set 1791290096 TIME 2026-10-06T12:34:56Z source=SET Sets the clock from Unix seconds. Logged as a CLOCK_SET event. time set 4294967295 TIME refused: reserved value The value means unset. Nothing changes. time set 17x Invalid argument reply Nothing changes. The clock uses the MCU clock. It has no temperature compensation, so it drifts with the crystal. The OBC should set it periodically. Modbus reads and sets the same clock: 40040 – 40041 to set and read, and 30039 – 30040 to read.

docs.text: Command example Expected reply Notes status STATUS , then the replies of mode , temp , telemetry , fault get , and bootinfo , one after another Read-only summary for the technician. Each section has the same format as its own command. reset confirm RESET outputs off, restarting Turns VOUT and TRANS off, sends the reply, then restarts the MCU through the watchdog after about 0.1 s. The next boot reports cause=COMMAND . Without confirm nothing happens. reset Invalid argument reply Needs confirm . persist_reset internal confirm PERSIST_RESET internal EEPROM erased, restarting Turns VOUT and TRANS off, blanks every byte of internal EEPROM (fault latch, limit error, limit values, boot record and history, config, clock checkpoint), then restarts the same way reset confirm does, since all of that is cached in RAM at boot and needs a fresh init to pick up the now-blank EEPROM. Blanking takes under a second on a lightly-used chip (it skips bytes that already read 0xFF), well inside the TPL5010's 10 s window. persist_reset external confirm PERSIST_RESET external EEPROM erased Blanks the whole U14 24C04 (the event log ring). Nothing is cached from it at boot, so this does not restart the MCU or touch the outputs. A failed erase (chip not acknowledging) replies PERSIST_RESET external EEPROM failed . persist_reset internal , persist_reset external , persist_reset Invalid or too-few-arguments reply Each needs its scope ( internal or external ) and confirm . persist_reset is the only command that returns EEPROM to the state of a never-written chip; fault clear , mode normal , and config_reset confirm each clear a narrower, specific piece of internal EEPROM state (see Mode state machine §8 and the configuration section above).

docs.text: Current firmware architecture This is the short overview of the DAL_PDU firmware. The detail lives in two pages: Code architecture : layers, dependencies, data flows, task inventory, shared state. Scheduler design : the task model, API, timing, concurrency rules, and limits. Target and entry point The Atmel Studio project is PDU/firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/ and targets the ATmega128A at 12 MHz. main.c calls APP_Main() in src/dev/M0_App/app_main.c , which initializes everything and then runs the main loop, which only dispatches SCH_HandleScheduledTask() . Modbus runs as a 5 ms task. Layers Layer Responsibility M0_App Startup, console, heartbeat LED, TRANS and fault handling, rail monitoring, watchdog supervision, Modbus callbacks. M1_Sys Scheduler (1 ms tick and task dispatch), CommandLine (parser and handlers), SystemData (shared status). M2_BSP Board pin map, UART ownership, timer ISR, I2C, power GPIO, watchdog, Modbus port, chip bindings. M3_Driver Component drivers (UART, software UART, I2C, GPIO) and chip drivers (TPS55287, PAC1934, 24C04). M4_MiddleWare Byte FIFO, printf hook, FreeMODBUS (submodule). Scheduled work Seven tasks run from the main loop, driven by a 1 ms Timer0 tick: console (10 ms), heartbeat (20 ms), TRANS fault check (6 ms), Modbus (5 ms), rail monitor (1000 ms), watchdog (10 ms), and board temperature (1000 ms). The full inventory, with phases and what each task reads and writes, is in Code architecture §4 . Interfaces UART0 (PE0/PE1) and the software console (PE3/PE4) both run at 9600 baud and share one command table. Each port has its own line buffer, and replies go back to the port that sent the command. See Current command reference . Modbus RTU runs as the configured slave (default 1) at the configured baud (default 9600) on USART1 (PD2/PD3, RS485 direction on PD5). See Modbus RTU implementation . I2C on PD0/PD1 serves the TPS55287 (VOUT), the PAC1934 monitor, and the 24C04 EEPROM. Power path TRANS is switched by the active-low PC2 eFuse. VOUT is enabled only while TRANS is on and both fault inputs are clear. A fault turns VOUT off first, then TRANS. The fault stays latched in internal EEPROM until it is cleared by command. The PAC1934 task records voltage, current, and power for VOUT, +12, +5_TRANS, and +5, but it does not yet enforce setpoint agreement or overcurrent limits. The mode (NORMAL, MANUAL, WARNING, or ERROR) gates TRANS. A missing regulator, or a limit trip in NORMAL, is ERROR. An unreadable PAC1934 or a latched fault is WARNING. Running drops outputs to off after 5 seconds without a Modbus request. See Mode state machine . Build and tests Open DAL_PDU.atsln in Atmel Studio 7 for the AVR build. From SOFTWARE , run make -C PDU/tests test for the host unit tests. Host tests do not replace bench checks of serial timing, output voltage, or fault wiring. Versioning and release The version and the build identity are described on the Versioning page under Code Implementation.

docs.text: Modbus RTU implementation The ATmega128A runs a Modbus RTU slave at the configured address ( 1 by default) and baud ( 9600 by default), 8N1 on USART1. RX is PD2, TX is PD3, and PD5 drives the RS485 direction line (high to transmit). Timer1 supplies the RTU silence interval. FreeMODBUS is a submodule under firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/src/dev/M4_MiddleWare/ThirdParty/freemodbus/ . Clone with git submodule update --init before building. Addresses below use conventional one-based Modbus notation. Subtract one for masters that expect zero-based request offsets: coil 00002 has offset 1 . Unsupported addresses return an illegal address exception. Other addresses in the design draft remain reserved. Events and clock The OBC reads an event in two steps. Write 40050 with the sequence number wanted ( 0 for the newest). Then read 30041 – 30047 . Poll 30041 alone to see when a new event arrives, since it changes with each event. The clock is set with 40040 – 40041 and read with 30039 – 30040 . Both use the same clock as the console time command. Check 30048 for the clock source: RESTORED means the time came from the last checkpoint and is approximate until the OBC sets it. The clock is checkpointed to EEPROM every 15 minutes. Scheduling The Modbus port is polled by a 5 ms task, not by the main loop. Each run calls eMBPoll twice, so a request is answered within about one period, which is 5 ms plus the length of the other tasks in that pass. The task also checks in with the watchdog (200 ms timeout). A request is a single frame, and the master waits for the reply, so polling every 5 ms is well inside any normal master response timeout. Keep any single task well under the 200 ms watchdog timeout, since a long task delays the Modbus reply. Disabling TRANS also requests VOUT off. 00003 CLEAR_FAULT_LATCH Read: 1 while any fault is latched. Write 1 to clear the latch in internal EEPROM. Write 0 does nothing. The latch does not enable TRANS. 00010 HEARTBEAT_ENABLE LED blinking enable. Applies to the NORMAL pattern only. Fault and warning indications always show. Coils 00001 and 00002 can be read or written together. In a two-coil write, bit 0 is VOUT and bit 1 is TRANS. Enabling VOUT while disabling TRANS is rejected. Enabling both turns TRANS on first; a failed VOUT enable rolls back a newly enabled TRANS branch. docs.text: Mode state machine This page describes the operating mode as implemented in M0_App/app_mode.c (2026-10-05). The mode is one of four: NORMAL , MANUAL , WARNING , and ERROR . The earlier four-state model (Standby, Running, ProtectedShutdown, SafeFault) is gone. 1. Modes Mode Value Entered when Outputs (VOUT, TRANS) Commands Regulator monitored NORMAL 0 No error, and no manual request Allowed. Limits act. All Yes MANUAL 1 Requested by command, from NORMAL, WARNING, or ERROR (revised 2026-10-15: outranks ERROR once requested) Allowed, including trans on / tps55287 on , regardless of a regulator/limit cause underneath. Limits log only. All No WARNING 2 The PAC1934 is unreadable, an I2C timeout is active, the VOUT setpoint readback mismatches, or Modbus link loss ( SRS-COM-045 ) Allowed. Link loss by itself does not turn outputs off. Limits log only. All Yes ERROR 3 The regulator (U5) does not respond when TRANS is enabled, or it faults or stops responding while TRANS is on; a limit trips in NORMAL; or an eFuse fault (PC4 for 12V TRANS, PC0 for 12V_MCU) reads continuously active for 50 ms (revised 2026-10-16, was WARNING — see SRS-PROT-020 ) Both off, unless MANUAL has since been requested All No The mode is derived on each call to AppMode_Get() . The first matching rule wins: MANUAL, if a manual request is active (revised 2026-10-15: checked before ERROR, so a manual request always wins — see OI-34). ERROR, if the regulator error flag, the limit error flag, or a latched eFuse fault is set (revised 2026-10-16: the eFuse latch moved here from WARNING — see OI-35). WARNING, if the PAC1934 is unreadable, an I2C timeout is active, the setpoint readback mismatches, or Modbus link loss is active. NORMAL otherwise. Every mode accepts all commands and responds. ERROR's causes (regulator, limit, and the eFuse latch) and MANUAL are independent flags: requesting MANUAL does not clear any of them, it only changes which one AppMode_Get() reports and which gates (like AppPower_SetTrans 's ERROR check, and the eFuse auto-shutdown in AppPower_ShutdownOnFault ) are satisfied. A healthy mode normal request clears regulator/limit causes; only fault clear removes an eFuse latch. Leaving MANUAL still requires an explicit mode normal request after clearing the latch. The regulator is not watched automatically in either MANUAL or ERROR. 2. Transitions From To Trigger Actions TRANS enable attempt ERROR Regulator not detected once TRANS is powered Both outputs off; TRANS is turned back off Startup WARNING PAC1934 not detected None Startup ERROR Limit ERROR flag stored from an earlier trip Both outputs off until a healthy mode normal request Startup NORMAL No error None NORMAL or WARNING ERROR Regulator status fault (SCP, OCP, or OVP), or regulator stops responding Both outputs off NORMAL ERROR Over-temperature or overcurrent limit exceeded for the required samples ( PROT-021 , PROT-022 ) Both outputs off. A confirmed eFuse fault behaves like any other ERROR cause for mode purposes (MANUAL still outranks it), but only fault clear removes its latch. Requests to enter MANUAL are never refused for this reason (revised 2026-10-15, OI-34). 3. Regulator monitor The one-second rail monitor ( AppPowerMonitor_Update ) reads the TPS55287 status register while the mode is NORMAL or WARNING and TRANS is on . The TPS55287 (U5) sits behind the TRANS eFuse and is unpowered whenever TRANS is off, so the monitor does not poll it then — polling an unpowered chip would otherwise read back as a failure and set ERROR for no reason. Any SCP, OCP, or OVP flag, or a failed read while TRANS is on, sets the ERROR flag. The flags are cleared by the read, so the monitor acts on the value it has just read. ERROR is cleared only by a healthy normal-mode request. The same reasoning applies to enabling TRANS: AppPower_SetTrans(true) and AppPower_EnsureRegulatorOn() (used by tps55287 set / on and the equivalent Modbus writes) probe the TPS55287 right after powering TRANS on, and set the ERROR flag (turning TRANS back off) if it does not answer. Right after that probe, they also write register 0x04 to external feedback ( 0x80 ) and read it back to confirm, since the chip resets to internal feedback every time its EN /UVLO drops — which happens on every TRANS power-cycle. This board wires an external divider (R22/R30, ratio ≈ 0.0997) rather than using the chip's internal ratio, so a failed readback there sets ERROR the same way a failed presence probe does. mode normal probes the regulator through AppPower_ProbeRegulator() when a regulator or limit ERROR is set, so it also works from a cold boot with TRANS off: it powers TRANS on just long enough to check (unless the eFuse fault is latched, in which case it refuses without touching TRANS), then restores TRANS to whatever it was before, whatever the result. That lets mode normal clear a persisted limit ERROR too, not only a regulator ERROR — AppMode_Retry requires both causes to be clear before it drops either one, so without this probe a stale limit ERROR left over from before a reset could never be cleared while TRANS was off. 4. Outputs ERROR : AppPower_Update turns VOUT off, then TRANS off, on every 6 ms pass while TRANS is on — unless MANUAL has been requested since, in which case outputs stay under manual control. TRANS cannot be enabled from ERROR itself (only from MANUAL, which outranks it). Link timeout ( SRS-COM-045 , revised 2026-10-15): if no Modbus request has arrived for the configured timeout (default 5 s) after the first one, this raises the link WARNING cause in mode get . It no longer turns VOUT or TRANS off by itself, and is not persisted (plain RAM state, cleared the instant a new valid Modbus request arrives). Previously this turned outputs off without changing the mode; that was reversed because in practice it was tripping during console-only bench use with no Modbus traffic at all, not an actual lost link in the field — see OI-03. Latched eFuse fault (revised 2026-10-16, SRS-PROT-020 ): PC4 (while TRANS is on) or PC0 must read continuously active for 50 ms before it is treated as real — a brief read, for example from inrush when TRANS switches on, resets the timer and never latches. Once confirmed, it is ERROR, not WARNING, and stays latched until fault clear , regardless of mode — enabling is refused by the latched record, checked in AppPower_SetTrans . While in MANUAL, a confirmed fault is still latched and reported ( fault get , and mode get 's latch= ), but AppPower_ShutdownOnFault no longer forces outputs off for it, matching every other ERROR cause once MANUAL has been requested. The live PC4/PC0 pins themselves are no longer checked at the moment of enabling (decided 2026-10-15): a fault that is live but not yet confirmed does not refuse a trans on / tps55287 on attempt by itself. The 6 ms AppPower_Update poll still reads the live pins every pass and, once the 50 ms debounce confirms a real fault, latches it and shuts TRANS back off (outside MANUAL) — so a fault that is still present gets caught and the output disabled within about 50 ms regardless; this only removes a synchronous pre-check that duplicated that poll on the same tick as the enable attempt. Each current needs three consecutive samples above it. Every trip is logged once as a WARNING event in the 24C04, whatever the mode. A trip is logged again only after the value has returned under the limit. In NORMAL, the trip also turns VOUT and then TRANS off and sets the limit ERROR. In MANUAL, WARNING, and ERROR, the trip only logs. Outputs are not changed. Limit ERROR end : mode normal clears it once the regulator responds and every limit is back in range. The flag is stored in internal EEPROM, so the ERROR survives a reset until that request succeeds. The health check does not leave an output on. 5. The TPS55287 (U5) sits behind the TRANS eFuse, which stays off at boot by design, so it cannot be probed here. It is not part of the startup self-test: it is checked on demand instead, the first time TRANS is enabled (see section 3 ). Refused if the check fails or an eFuse fault is latched. mode manual Requests MANUAL. Never refused for being in ERROR (revised 2026-10-15, OI-34) — the regulator/limit/latch cause, if any, is untouched underneath. limit , limit temp <tenths C> , limit vout <mA> , limit trans <mA> Shows or sets the limits. Stored in internal EEPROM. config , config set address , config set baud , config set timeout , config_reset confirm Shows or sets the Modbus address, baud, and communications timeout, or restores all settings to the defaults. See Command reference . event get Lists the events in the 24C04 ring, with the clock time. Modbus input 30022 Mode value: 0 NORMAL, 1 MANUAL, 2 WARNING, 3 ERROR. Modbus holding 40030 Read: mode value. Write 0 requests NORMAL, 1 requests MANUAL. Modbus holding 40031 – 40033 Limits: temperature in tenths of a degree C (signed), VOUT in mA, +5_TRANS in mA. A refused write returns an exception. 8. Known limits The limit defaults are 85.0 °C for two samples, and 1000 mA for three samples on VOUT and on +5_TRANS. They need bench confirmation. The values are in the ATmega128A internal EEPROM, as SRS-CFG-060 now requires (OI-11). A limit ERROR is kept across a reset in internal EEPROM. It clears on a healthy mode normal request, once the limits are back in range. The Modbus limit registers 40031 – 40033 are in the implemented map. The design draft has no equivalent (OI-14). The startup self-test checks that the PAC1934 and 24C04 acknowledge. It does not check their configuration, and it no longer includes the TPS55287 (see section 5 ). The regulator presence check now runs on demand, the first time TRANS is enabled after boot or after being turned off, rather than at startup. Nothing currently re-arms the TPS55287's own registers (feedback mode, voltage reference) after TRANS has been power-cycled; only its presence is re-checked. The link timeout raises the link WARNING cause and no longer turns outputs off by itself (revised 2026-10-15; see the open question below, now resolved). In MANUAL it sets only the WARNING cause ( bus=1 in mode ), and the mode stays MANUAL. A timeout from any other device sets WARNING until a transaction completes. A NACK from an absent device is not a fault. The bootloader is not implemented, so there is no bootloader mode. 9. Open question Link timeout (Q7 follow-up) — resolved 2026-10-15. docs.text: This page describes the operating mode as implemented in M0_App/app_mode.c (2026-10-05). The mode is one of four: NORMAL , MANUAL , WARNING , and ERROR . The earlier four-state model (Standby, Running, ProtectedShutdown, SafeFault) is gone.

docs.text: Open issues This page lists the work still open against the requirements, use cases, and user stories in Software requirements and Use cases, user stories & commands . Status is as of 2026-10-05, checked against the firmware. The per-requirement status tables are in Software requirements §7 . Priority is set by safety impact first, then by how much other work depends on the item. High : affects protection, failsafe behavior, or a use case the OBC relies on. Medium : needed for the requirement to be fully met, but the system is still safe without it. Low : documentation, verification, or cleanup. High priority ID Issue Requirements Use cases / stories Next step OI-01 Resolved 2026-10-05. Fault latch and clear. A fault that switches TRANS off is latched in the ATmega128A internal EEPROM and survives reset. PROT-023 , PROT-020 UC-4 ; "fault latches" story Cleared by Modbus coil 00003 or fault clear . trans on is refused while latched. See Modbus RTU implementation and Current command reference . OI-02 Resolved 2026-10-05. Mode model: NORMAL, MANUAL, WARNING, and ERROR. The mode is derived from the regulator flag, the limit error, the manual request, the PAC1934 status, and the fault latch. PWR-011 , PWR-015 , PROT-050 , MON-033 UC-8 Revise PROT-050 in the SRS, since the retry command now exits ERROR. Bootloader mode is still open under OI-16. See Mode state machine . OI-03 Resolved 2026-10-05, revised 2026-10-15. Modbus link loss (default 5 s without a request) is now a WARNING cause ( mode get 's link= ) and no longer turns outputs off or latches anything by itself; see SRS-COM-045 . Previously it turned VOUT and the transducer branch off while leaving the mode unchanged — decided to drop that, since the only thing that was tripping it in practice was console-only bench use with no Modbus traffic, not a real lost-link condition in the field. COM-045 , WDT-080 "fail safe on lost Modbus" story Watchdog client coverage for Modbus is still open under OI-08. If a real field deployment needs the output shutdown back, it would need to be reintroduced deliberately, not inferred from this entry. OI-04 Resolved 2026-10-05 with defaults. Overcurrent in NORMAL mode: 1000 mA on VOUT (decided 2026-10-06) or +5_TRANS for three samples turns outputs off, enters ERROR, and logs a WARNING event. Limits are set with limit and stored in internal EEPROM. PROT-022 , CFG-060 UC-4 Confirm the default on the bench. The limits are on Modbus 40031 – 40033 . The map is aligned under OI-14. OI-05 Resolved 2026-10-05 with defaults. Over-temperature in NORMAL mode: 85.0 °C for two samples turns outputs off, enters ERROR, and logs a WARNING event. The threshold is set with limit temp and stored in internal EEPROM. PROT-021 , CFG-060 UC-4 Confirm the default on the bench. The threshold is on Modbus 40031 . The map is aligned under OI-14. OI-06 Resolved 2026-10-06. The rail monitor checks the PAC1934 VOUT voltage against the commanded setpoint once a second, while TRANS and VOUT are on. Each judged sample must be within 5 % of the setpoint (at least 100 mV). Three judged samples out of tolerance flag a WARNING and log SETPOINT_MISMATCH . The first two checks after a change are not judged. PWR-014 , COM-040 UC-1 ; "read back actual voltage" story None open. Confirm the tolerance and settling on the bench. OI-31 Resolved 2026-10-15. The TPS55287 (U5) is behind the TRANS eFuse, which stays off at boot by design, so it could not answer the startup self-test, which unconditionally latched ERROR on every boot and then blocked trans on / tps55287 on from ever succeeding ( AppMode_Get() != APP_MODE_ERROR gates AppPower_SetTrans(true) ). The one-second rail monitor made it worse: it kept polling the TPS55287 even while TRANS was correctly off at idle, re-latching ERROR on the first pass. The self-test no longer probes the TPS55287; the regulator is instead checked on demand ( AppPower_EnsureRegulatorOn ) the first time TRANS is enabled, from trans on , tps55287 set / on , or the equivalent Modbus writes (coil 00001 , holding 40001 ). The rail monitor now only polls while TRANS is on. mode retry had the same deadlock one level up: it probed the chip directly ( BSP_TPS55287_Detect ) without powering TRANS, so regulator_ok was always false while TRANS was off, and since AppMode_Retry only clears a cause when both the regulator and the limits check out, a persisted limit ERROR from before a reset (EEPROM-backed, unrelated to the regulator) could never be cleared either as long as TRANS stayed off. mode retry now calls AppPower_ProbeRegulator() , which powers TRANS just long enough to probe (skipping the probe entirely if the eFuse fault is latched) and restores it to how it was found either way. PWR-011 , PROT-050 UC-1 , UC-8 None open. Re-arming the TPS55287's feedback/voltage registers after a power-cycle is now done too (OI-32). See Mode state machine . OI-32 Resolved 2026-10-15. This board wires an external feedback divider (R22 = 102 kΩ, R30 = 11.3 kΩ to GND; ratio ≈ 0.0997, confirmed on hardware), but the TPS55287 resets to internal feedback (register 0x04 = 0x03 ) every time its EN /UVLO drops, and nothing ever wrote that register — so after any TRANS power-cycle (the normal idle-off case, every time, after OI-31), the chip was running the wrong ratio. The driver rejected the external case outright ( TPS55287_SetVoltageMv / GetVoltageMv returned false whenever the FB bit was set), so this was invisible rather than dangerous as long as nothing wrote register 0x04 to 0x80 manually; if it had been written, the chip would have used the external ratio's math nowhere in the firmware, risking the wrong output voltage (see the TPS55287 safety review discussion, ~21 V from a 12 V command in the worst case). TPS55287_SetVoltageMv / GetVoltageMv now compute against either ratio, selected by the FB bit already read from the chip. AppPower_SetTrans(true) / AppPower_EnsureRegulatorOn() now write register 0x04 to 0x80 and read it back to confirm, right after the presence probe, every time TRANS powers on — so the chip is always in external feedback before tps55287 set / on or the equivalent Modbus write can run. PWR-010 , PWR-013 , assumption A-4 UC-1 Confirm the 0.0997 ratio and the ~12 V range against a bench measurement, per A-4 ; the resistor values are not yet independently verified beyond what was reported. docs.text: Scheduler design This page documents the scheduler in PDU/firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/src/dev/M1_Sys/Scheduler/ ( scheduler.c , scheduler.h , scheduler_define.h ) as it exists today. It covers the model, the data each task carries, the rules for which context may touch which field, the timing it gives, and its known limits. The code architecture around it is in Code architecture . 1. Model The scheduler is a per-task-period, non-preemptive dispatcher : A 1 ms tick, driven by Timer0's compare interrupt, advances every registered task's own counter. When a counter reaches the task's period, the task is marked ready . The tick never runs the task. The main loop calls SCH_HandleScheduledTask() . That call runs every ready task once, in table index order. Each task has its own period, phase, and enable flag. Periods are not tied to a shared step grid. Tasks have no priority . Ordering is by table index only, and a running task is never preempted. Both halves are needed: the tick decides what is due, the main loop decides when it runs. The scheduler is not a cyclic executive. A cyclic executive derives each task's rate from a fixed step table, so every rate is a multiple of one step. docs.title: Scheduler design

docs.text: The scheduler is a per-task-period, non-preemptive dispatcher : A 1 ms tick, driven by Timer0's compare interrupt, advances every registered task's own counter. When a counter reaches the task's period, the task is marked ready . The tick never runs the task. The main loop calls SCH_HandleScheduledTask() . That call runs every ready task once, in table index order. Each task has its own period, phase, and enable flag. Periods are not tied to a shared step grid. Tasks have no priority . Ordering is by table index only, and a running task is never preempted. Both halves are needed: the tick decides what is due, the main loop decides when it runs. The scheduler is not a cyclic executive. A cyclic executive derives each task's rate from a fixed step table, so every rate is a multiple of one step. The trade-off is discussed in Design trade-offs .

docs.text:
Software requirements document 1. Scope This document defines the requirements for the DAL_PDU firmware (ATmega128A, U6 ). The firmware turns the board into an OBC-commanded variable power supply: it regulates and reports the VOUT rail, switches the transducer branch, reports telemetry, accepts commands over Modbus (RS-485), a PC104 UART, and a local console UART, and hosts a dual-bank, CRC-checked bootloader that the OBC can use to reflash the board over the PC104 UART. Hardware facts referenced here come from Hardware overview ; see that page for the underlying schematic evidence. Requirement IDs use the prefix SRS-<AREA>-<NNN> . AREA is one of GEN (general), PWR (power control), PROT (protection), MON (monitoring), COM (communications), BOOT (bootloader), WDT (watchdog), CFG (configuration/NVM). 2. Assumptions and hardware dependencies ID Assumption Consequence if false A-1 IF-001 (RS-232 driver/receiver direction at U12) is corrected before firmware bring-up. The console uses the software UART on PE3/PE4 ( MCU-001 , decided). Section 4.1's allocation of USART0 to the PC104 UART is valid once IF-001 is fixed. The PC104 UART and bootloader cannot function until then. A-2 The crystal is 12 MHz and the I2C pull-ups are 4.7 kΩ, as fitted ( BOM-002 , I2C-001 , decided 2026-10-06). The BOM and schematic are brought into line with this ( BOM-001 , BOM-003 ). Baud-rate, I2C, ADC, and timer calculations use F_CPU = 12 MHz in dal_pdu_board.h . The Timer0 tick is 1.0027 ms (0.27 % slow). Baud errors are 0.16 % or less. A-3 IF-002 (RS-485 idle bias about 30 mV) is accepted as-is (decided 2026-10-06). Modbus framing must tolerate line noise during idle and undriven bus periods ( SRS-COM-030 ). A-4 The TPS55287 output range, feedback scaling, and I2C register map are confirmed against the built board. Feedback topology is confirmed external (R22 = 102 kΩ, R30 = 11.3 kΩ to GND; ratio ≈ 0.0997), not yet independently bench-measured/calibrated per the hardware review's power page. VOUT setpoint units and range in this document (Section 4.2) are provisional until calibrated A-5 No hardware power-good signal is used for the fixed 5 V rails. The PG outputs are unused by decision ( PWR-004 ). Rail-health inference relies entirely on PAC1934 readings, not a GPIO power-good interrupt 3. System modes The operating mode is one of four: NORMAL , MANUAL , WARNING , and ERROR . The mode is derived from the self-test, the fault latch, the manual request, and the PAC1934 status. The implementation is described in Mode state machine . stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> NORMAL: startup, no error [*] --> WARNING: PAC1934 U10 not detected NORMAL --> WARNING: PAC1934 unreadable or link lost NORMAL --> ERROR: over-temperature or overcurrent limit WARNING --> NORMAL: cause clears NORMAL --> ERROR: regulator not detected when TRANS is enabled, fault, or no response WARNING --> ERROR: regulator not detected when TRANS is enabled, fault, or no response NORMAL --> MANUAL: manual request WARNING --> MANUAL: manual request ERROR --> MANUAL: manual request MANUAL --> NORMAL: normal request, regulator responds and no limit is exceeded ERROR --> NORMAL: normal request, healthy regulator and limits ERROR --> WARNING: normal request, healthy regulator and limits; warning cause present The regulator (U5) is behind the TRANS eFuse, which is off at idle by design, so it is checked on demand the first time TRANS is enabled, not at startup (OI-31) — the [*] --> ERROR transition that used to exist here for a missing regulator at startup is gone for that reason. NORMAL : outputs allowed, as commanded. The regulator is monitored every second. A regulator fault, or an over-temperature or overcurrent limit trip, moves the unit to ERROR. MANUAL : entered by command from NORMAL, WARNING, or ERROR. A confirmed eFuse fault is latched and reported without a software shutdown of VOUT or TRANS. Regulator and limit causes also leave outputs under operator control. A normal request checks regulator and limits before leaving MANUAL; an eFuse latch must first be cleared with fault clear . WARNING : entered when the PAC1934 is unreadable or Modbus link loss is active. Link loss by itself does not turn outputs off. ERROR : entered for a regulator fault, a limit trip in NORMAL, or a confirmed eFuse fault outside MANUAL. Outputs are forced off. A normal request clears regulator/limit causes only after a successful health check; an eFuse latch requires fault clear . Self-test (startup only): U10 missing gives WARNING, and U14 (24C04) missing is recorded but does not change the mode. U5 is not part of the startup self-test (OI-31) — it is checked on demand the first time TRANS is enabled. Bootloader : not yet implemented (see Open issues OI-16 ). When implemented, VOUT and the transducer branch are forced off before entry ( SRS-BOOT-076 ). 4. Functional requirements 4.1 Serial resource allocation The MCU has two hardware USARTs and three required serial roles (Section 3 of Hardware overview ). This design allocates them by criticality: the OBC-facing Modbus link is the primary real-time control channel and gets a hardware UART even though it is not the one silk-screened for it; the human-operated console tolerates a software UART's jitter. Requirement Statement SRS-COM-001 The PC104 UART (commands + bootloader, H1-19/20 via U12) shall use USART0 ( PE0 / PE1 ), once IF-001 is corrected. No pin change required. SRS-COM-002 The Modbus/RS-485 link shall use USART1 : MCU RX on PD2 , MCU TX on PD3 , and the RS-485 direction on PD5 , as wired on the board (ECO confirmed 2026-10-06). SRS-COM-003 Superseded by SRS-COM-002 . The ECO is on the board, so the bit-banged Modbus fallback is not used. SRS-COM-004 The local console ( P2 , MCU_CONSOLE_TX/RX on PE3 / PE4 ) shall be implemented as a timer-driven, bit-banged UART on those existing pins, since they are not a hardware USART pair ( MCU-001 ) and the console is human-typed, low-duty, and non-real-time. SRS-COM-030 With the RS-485 idle bias at about 30 mV ( A-3 ), the firmware shall accept a request only when its frame is complete (T3.5 silence), its address matches, and its CRC is valid. Bytes that do not form a valid frame shall be discarded without a reply. SRS-COM-005 The debug UART ( P1 , sharing USART0 logic) shall be bench/ground-only and shall not be active at the same time as the PC104 UART in a flight/operational configuration. 4.2 Power control (variable output) Requirement Statement SRS-PWR-010 Firmware shall command the VOUT setpoint by writing the U5 TPS55287 output-voltage register over the shared I2C/TWI bus ( PD0 / PD1 ). SRS-PWR-011 Firmware shall default VOUT and the transducer branch ( U1 ) to disabled at power-up, until commanded otherwise. SRS-PWR-012 Firmware shall enable the transducer branch ( U1 via MCU_EFUSE_EN /Q1) before enabling VOUT , and shall disable VOUT before disabling the transducer branch, on every transition. SRS-PWR-013 Firmware shall use the board's external feedback configuration ( 0x04 = 0x80 ) before calculating a setpoint or enabling VOUT, verify that configuration over I2C, and reject setpoints outside 800–12000 mV rather than clamping silently. If VOUT is already enabled in the wrong feedback mode, it shall be disabled before correction. The range remains subject to bench calibration (Assumption A-4 ). SRS-PWR-014 Firmware shall confirm the applied VOUT setpoint by reading back the PAC1934 VOUT channel within a bounded settling time and flag a setpoint-mismatch condition if the measured value does not converge. SRS-PWR-015 Revised 2026-10-15 (added the MANUAL exception to the ERROR clause). Firmware shall not enable VOUT or the transducer branch in ERROR — unless a manual request has since been made, in which case MANUAL shall take priority and enabling shall be allowed — while a fault is latched, or while the bootloader is active (Section 3). The latched-fault and bootloader clauses are not affected by a manual request. 4.3 Protection Requirement Statement SRS-PROT-020 Revised 2026-10-16 (debounce added; WARNING changed to ERROR). Firmware shall monitor EFUSE1_MCU_FLT and EFUSE2_MCU_FLT . Assertion shall be confirmed only once continuous for 50 ms (a brief assertion, for example from inrush when TRANS switches, shall not latch). Once confirmed, it shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off, latch the fault ( SRS-PROT-023 ), and enter ERROR — unless a manual request has since been made ( SRS-PROT-050 ), in which case the fault shall still be latched and reported but shall not force outputs off. SRS-PROT-021 In NORMAL mode, firmware shall monitor board temperature ( TC1047A , PF1 /ADC1) against an over-temperature limit (default 85.0 °C, set with the limit command and stored in internal EEPROM). After two consecutive samples at or above the limit, it shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off and enter ERROR. In every mode, each trip shall be logged as a WARNING event ( SRS-MON-032 ). SRS-PROT-022 In NORMAL mode, firmware shall monitor PAC1934 current readings on the VOUT and +5_TRANS channels against limits (default 1000 mA each, set with the limit command and stored in internal EEPROM). After three consecutive samples above a limit, it shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off and enter ERROR. In every mode, each trip shall be logged as a WARNING event ( SRS-MON-032 ). The check is independent of the eFuse's own hardware current limit. SRS-PROT-023 A latched fault shall remain latched until cleared by command: Modbus coil 00003 or the fault clear console command. The clear shall be refused while a fault input is still active. Firmware shall not auto-clear a latched fault. SRS-PROT-024 Because U2 (MCU branch) cannot be switched off by firmware, a fault on the MCU branch itself shall be reported but cannot be remediated by firmware power-cycling itself; only telemetry/fault reporting applies. SRS-PROT-050 When the regulator check fails, or a limit trips ( SRS-PROT-021 , SRS-PROT-022 ), outputs shall be off outside MANUAL. MANUAL takes priority and leaves outputs under operator control. A request for NORMAL shall clear regulator/limit causes only after the regulator responds and no limit is exceeded. An eFuse latch is cleared separately by fault clear ( SRS-PROT-023 ). The firmware shall not reset itself to clear ERROR. 4.4 Monitoring / telemetry Requirement Statement SRS-MON-030 Firmware shall poll all four PAC1934 channels ( VOUT , +12 input, +5_TRANS , +5 ) at a fixed background rate independent of communications activity. SRS-MON-031 Firmware shall sample board temperature at a fixed background rate and make the latest reading available on every communications channel. SRS-MON-032 Firmware shall keep a bounded persistent event log (a 32-slot ring in the 24C04) of fault, mode, and limit events, each stamped with the software clock ( SRS-MON-034 ), retrievable via console and Modbus. SRS-MON-033 Telemetry values shall be available (read-only) in every mode, including ERROR and WARNING, so a fault remains observable after it occurs. SRS-MON-034 Firmware shall keep a software clock (UTC), set from the console ( time set ) or Modbus ( 40040 – 40041 ) and read from either. The clock shall store a checkpoint in internal EEPROM every 15 minutes and on each set, and shall restore the last checkpoint after a reset, marked as RESTORED . Each logged event shall carry the clock time and its source ( UNSET , RESTORED , or SET ). 4.5 Communications (general) Requirement Statement SRS-COM-040 The Modbus interface shall implement a Modbus RTU slave per the register map in Modbus RTU implementation . The design draft differences are in Design differences . SRS-COM-041 The Modbus slave address shall be stored in non-volatile configuration ( SRS-CFG-061 ) and take effect only after reboot. SRS-COM-042 The PC104 UART shall implement the ASCII command set in Use cases & commands plus the bootloader wire protocol (Section 6). SRS-COM-043 The console UART shall implement the same ASCII command set as the PC104 UART, plus maintenance-only commands not exposed to the OBC (e.g. forced bank swap), listed in the same reference table. SRS-COM-044 Any command that changes VOUT state, transducer-branch state, or configuration shall be accepted from at most one channel's request at a time; firmware shall serialize command handling so Modbus, PC104 UART, and console cannot race each other. SRS-COM-045 Revised 2026-10-15 (previously: shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off, and the mode shall not change). Firmware shall enforce a communications watchdog: if no valid Modbus request is received for a timeout (default 5 s, configurable under SRS-CFG-060 ) after the first request, it shall raise a WARNING cause ( mode get 's link= ), at the same priority as the other WARNING causes (below ERROR and MANUAL). It shall not turn VOUT or the transducer branch off by itself. A new valid request clears the cause. 4.6 Bootloader and firmware update See Section 6 for the full flash layout and protocol design. Requirement Statement SRS-BOOT-070 The MCU flash shall be partitioned into a fixed, immutable boot section and two equally-sized application banks (Section 6.1). SRS-BOOT-071 Each application bank shall carry a header with image length, CRC32, firmware version, and a validity flag (Section 6.2). SRS-BOOT-072 On every reset, the boot section shall validate the CRC32 of the currently active bank before jumping to it; on validation failure it shall fall back to the other bank if that bank validates; if neither validates, it shall remain in bootloader mode and report the failure over the PC104 UART and console (Section 6.3). SRS-BOOT-073 The bootloader shall accept a new image only over the PC104 UART, using the framed protocol in Section 6.4, and shall not accept firmware images over Modbus or the console. SRS-BOOT-074 The bootloader shall write a new image to the inactive bank, verify its CRC32 after write, and only then mark it valid and switch the active-bank pointer — the previously active bank shall remain untouched and valid throughout the update. SRS-BOOT-075 New application firmware shall call a "confirm boot" routine within a bounded number of watchdog services after startup; if a newly activated bank fails to confirm within that window, the bootloader shall revert the active-bank pointer to the previous bank on the next reset (automatic rollback). SRS-BOOT-076 Entry into bootloader mode from running application code shall first force VOUT and the transducer branch to disabled ( SRS-PWR-015 ). 4.7 Watchdog Requirement Statement SRS-WDT-080 Firmware shall service the TPL5010 ( DONE pulse, PB6 ) only from a supervisory loop that has confirmed the main control loop, communications handling, and telemetry sampling are all progressing — not from a free-running timer interrupt alone. SRS-WDT-081 A TPL5010-forced reset shall be distinguishable, on the next boot, from a power-cycle or command-issued reset, and shall be recorded in the event log and exposed as a telemetry value (reset-reason code). SRS-WDT-082 Because U2 (MCU branch) is always powered, a TPL5010 reset shall be sufficient on its own to recover from a hung application without requiring a full power cycle. 4.8 Configuration and non-volatile storage Requirement Statement SRS-CFG-060 Configurable operating parameters (over-temperature threshold, overcurrent limits, Modbus slave address and baud code, communications-watchdog timeout) shall be stored in non-volatile memory. The over-temperature and overcurrent limits shall be stored in the ATmega128A internal EEPROM with a checksum, and the other parameters in the same internal EEPROM, in their own record (OI-11). SRS-CFG-061 The active-bank pointer and per-bank valid/confirmed flags (Section 6.2) shall be stored in EEPROM, separate from the application banks' own in-flash headers, so a corrupted flash bank cannot also corrupt the selector. SRS-CFG-062 Firmware shall ship compiled-in safe defaults for every EEPROM-backed parameter and fall back to them if EEPROM read fails or fails a checksum. SRS-CFG-063 Write-protect ( EE_WP ) shall be asserted by default and only deasserted for the duration of an explicit configuration-write command. 5. Non-functional requirements Requirement Statement SRS-GEN-090 The main control loop period shall be bounded and documented, and shall be short enough that the communications-watchdog timeout ( SRS-COM-045 ) and TPL5010 service interval ( SRS-WDT-080 ) are both met with margin. SRS-GEN-091 All shared-resource access (I2C bus to U5/U10/U14; EEPROM; command dispatch across the three serial channels) shall be protected against interrupt-context and multi-channel races. SRS-GEN-092 Firmware shall build with a documented toolchain/version and shall record the resulting firmware version and build identifier in each application bank's header ( SRS-BOOT-071 ) and in telemetry. SRS-GEN-093 No requirement in this document overrides a hardware protection function (eFuse current limit, TPL5010 reset); firmware protections in Section 4.3 are supplementary, not a replacement. 6. Bootloader design detail 6.1 Flash layout (ATmega128A, 128 KiB total) Region Address range Size Contents Bank A 0x00000 – 0x0EFFF 60 KiB Application image A + header Bank B 0x0F000 – 0x1DFFF 60 KiB Application image B + header Boot section 0x1E000 – 0x1FFFF 8 KiB Immutable bootloader ( BOOTSZ fuses), entered on every reset ( BOOTRST fuse) The boot section is written once during initial programming (via JTAG/ISP) and is not modified by the field-update protocol in Section 6.4 — only Bank A and Bank B are ever rewritten by the OBC. 6.2 Bank header Each bank begins with a fixed-size header, immediately followed by the application image: Field Size Description magic 4 bytes Fixed constant identifying a valid header (distinguishes "erased/blank" from "written") image_len 4 bytes Length of the application image in bytes image_crc32 4 bytes CRC32 of the application image (not including the header) fw_version 2 bytes Major/minor firmware version build_id 4 bytes Build number or timestamp valid 1 byte Set only after a successful post-write CRC verification ( SRS-BOOT-074 ) confirmed 1 byte Set by the application itself after boot ( SRS-BOOT-075 ); cleared by the bootloader when it activates a bank reserved remaining bytes to a round header size Padding for future fields The active-bank pointer and per-bank valid / confirmed mirror flags also live in EEPROM ( SRS-CFG-061 ) so the bootloader's bank-selection decision does not depend solely on reading flash that may itself be the thing that is corrupted. 6.3 Boot / fallback state machine flowchart TD START["Reset"] --> READPTR["Read active-bank pointer (EEPROM)"] READPTR --> CHKACTIVE{"Active bank
header valid + CRC OK?"} CHKACTIVE -->|yes| CHKCONFIRM{"Bank confirmed
within last run?"} CHKACTIVE -->|no| CHKOTHER{"Other bank
header valid + CRC OK?"} CHKCONFIRM -->|yes| JUMP["Jump to active bank"] CHKCONFIRM -->|no, previous run never confirmed| SWITCHBACK["Revert pointer to other bank"] --> CHKOTHER CHKOTHER -->|yes| ACTIVATE["Set other bank active, clear confirmed flag"] --> JUMP CHKOTHER -->|no| STAY["Remain in bootloader mode,
report failure on PC104 UART/console"] 6.4 Field update protocol (PC104 UART) Framed, binary protocol carried over the PC104 UART ( USART0 , once IF-001 is corrected). The bootloader only accepts this protocol on the PC104 UART, never on Modbus or the console ( SRS-BOOT-073 ). Frame format: Field Size Description SOF 1 byte Fixed start-of-frame marker CMD 1 byte Command code (below) LEN 2 bytes Payload length PAYLOAD LEN bytes Command-specific data CRC16 2 bytes CRC16 over CMD + LEN + PAYLOAD Commands: Command Direction Purpose PING OBC → PDU Liveness check; PDU replies with ACK GET_INFO OBC → PDU PDU replies with active bank, per-bank version/valid/confirmed status ERASE_BANK OBC → PDU Erase the inactive bank only (bootloader refuses to erase the active bank) WRITE_PAGE OBC → PDU Write one flash page (offset + data) into the inactive bank; PDU replies ACK / NACK per page FINALIZE_BANK OBC → PDU Supply final image length + CRC32; bootloader verifies, sets valid on success ACTIVATE_BANK OBC → PDU Switch the active-bank pointer to the just-written bank, clear its confirmed flag REBOOT OBC → PDU Reset the MCU, re-entering the state machine in Section 6.3 Update sequence: PING → GET_INFO → ERASE_BANK (inactive) → repeated WRITE_PAGE → FINALIZE_BANK → ACTIVATE_BANK → REBOOT . If the OBC never issues REBOOT , the previously active bank keeps running uninterrupted ( SRS-BOOT-074 ), and if the newly activated bank never calls its confirm routine after reboot, the rollback in Section 6.3 restores the previous bank automatically ( SRS-BOOT-075 ). 7. docs.text: This document defines the requirements for the DAL_PDU firmware (ATmega128A, U6 ). The firmware turns the board into an OBC-commanded variable power supply: it regulates and reports the VOUT rail, switches the transducer branch, reports telemetry, accepts commands over Modbus (RS-485), a PC104 UART, and a local console UART, and hosts a dual-bank, CRC-checked bootloader that the OBC can use to reflash the board over the PC104 UART. Hardware facts referenced here come from Hardware overview ; see that page for the underlying schematic evidence. Requirement IDs use the prefix SRS-<AREA>-<NNN> . AREA is one of GEN (general), PWR (power control), PROT (protection), MON (monitoring), COM (communications), BOOT (bootloader), WDT (watchdog), CFG (configuration/NVM).

docs.text: ID Assumption Consequence if false A-1 IF-001 (RS-232 driver/receiver direction at U12) is corrected before firmware bring-up. The console uses the software UART on PE3/PE4 ( MCU-001 , decided). Section 4.1's allocation of USART0 to the PC104 UART is valid once IF-001 is fixed. The PC104 UART and bootloader cannot function until then. A-2 The crystal is 12 MHz and the I2C pull-ups are 4.7 kΩ, as fitted ( BOM-002 , I2C-001 , decided 2026-10-06). The BOM and schematic are brought into line with this ( BOM-001 , BOM-003 ). Baud-rate, I2C, ADC, and timer calculations use F_CPU = 12 MHz in dal_pdu_board.h . The Timer0 tick is 1.0027 ms (0.27 % slow). Baud errors are 0.16 % or less. A-3 IF-002 (RS-485 idle bias about 30 mV) is accepted as-is (decided 2026-10-06). A-4 The TPS55287 output range, feedback scaling, and I2C register map are confirmed against the built board. Feedback topology is confirmed external (R22 = 102 kΩ, R30 = 11.3 kΩ to GND; ratio ≈ 0.0997), not yet independently bench-measured/calibrated per the hardware review's power page. docs.text: The operating mode is one of four: NORMAL , MANUAL , WARNING , and ERROR . The mode is derived from the self-test, the fault latch, the manual request, and the PAC1934 status. The implementation is described in Mode state machine . stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> NORMAL: startup, no error [*] --> WARNING: PAC1934 U10 not detected NORMAL --> WARNING: PAC1934 unreadable or link lost NORMAL --> ERROR: over-temperature or overcurrent limit WARNING --> NORMAL: cause clears NORMAL --> ERROR: regulator not detected when TRANS is enabled, fault, or no response WARNING --> ERROR: regulator not detected when TRANS is enabled, fault, or no response NORMAL --> MANUAL: manual request WARNING --> MANUAL: manual request ERROR --> MANUAL: manual request MANUAL --> NORMAL: normal request, regulator responds and no limit is exceeded ERROR --> NORMAL: normal request, healthy regulator and limits ERROR --> WARNING: normal request, healthy regulator and limits; warning cause present The regulator (U5) is behind the TRANS eFuse, which is off at idle by design, so it is checked on demand the first time TRANS is enabled, not at startup (OI-31) — the [*] --> ERROR transition that used to exist here for a missing regulator at startup is gone for that reason. NORMAL : outputs allowed, as commanded. The regulator is monitored every second. A regulator fault, or an over-temperature or overcurrent limit trip, moves the unit to ERROR. MANUAL : entered by command from NORMAL, WARNING, or ERROR. A confirmed eFuse fault is latched and reported without a software shutdown of VOUT or TRANS. Regulator and limit causes also leave outputs under operator control. A normal request checks regulator and limits before leaving MANUAL; an eFuse latch must first be cleared with fault clear . WARNING : entered when the PAC1934 is unreadable or Modbus link loss is active. Link loss by itself does not turn outputs off. ERROR : entered for a regulator fault, a limit trip in NORMAL, or a confirmed eFuse fault outside MANUAL. Outputs are forced off. A normal request clears regulator/limit causes only after a successful health check; an eFuse latch requires fault clear . Self-test (startup only): U10 missing gives WARNING, and U14 (24C04) missing is recorded but does not change the mode. U5 is not part of the startup self-test (OI-31) — it is checked on demand the first time TRANS is enabled. Bootloader : not yet implemented (see Open issues OI-16 ). When implemented, VOUT and the transducer branch are forced off before entry ( SRS-BOOT-076 ).

docs.text: The MCU has two hardware USARTs and three required serial roles (Section 3 of Hardware overview ). This design allocates them by criticality: the OBC-facing Modbus link is the primary real-time control channel and gets a hardware UART even though it is not the one silk-screened for it; the human-operated console tolerates a software UART's jitter. Requirement Statement SRS-COM-001 The PC104 UART (commands + bootloader, H1-19/20 via U12) shall use USART0 ( PE0 / PE1 ), once IF-001 is corrected. No pin change required. SRS-COM-002 The Modbus/RS-485 link shall use USART1 : MCU RX on PD2 , MCU TX on PD3 , and the RS-485 direction on PD5 , as wired on the board (ECO confirmed 2026-10-06). SRS-COM-003 Superseded by SRS-COM-002 . The ECO is on the board, so the bit-banged Modbus fallback is not used. SRS-COM-004 The local console ( P2 , MCU_CONSOLE_TX/RX on PE3 / PE4 ) shall be implemented as a timer-driven, bit-banged UART on those existing pins, since they are not a hardware USART pair ( MCU-001 ) and the console is human-typed, low-duty, and non-real-time. SRS-COM-030 With the RS-485 idle bias at about 30 mV ( A-3 ), the firmware shall accept a request only when its frame is complete (T3.5 silence), its address matches, and its CRC is valid. Bytes that do not form a valid frame shall be discarded without a reply. SRS-COM-005 The debug UART ( P1 , sharing USART0 logic) shall be bench/ground-only and shall not be active at the same time as the PC104 UART in a flight/operational configuration.

docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-PWR-010 Firmware shall command the VOUT setpoint by writing the U5 TPS55287 output-voltage register over the shared I2C/TWI bus ( PD0 / PD1 ). SRS-PWR-011 Firmware shall default VOUT and the transducer branch ( U1 ) to disabled at power-up, until commanded otherwise. SRS-PWR-012 Firmware shall enable the transducer branch ( U1 via MCU_EFUSE_EN /Q1) before enabling VOUT , and shall disable VOUT before disabling the transducer branch, on every transition. SRS-PWR-013 Firmware shall use the board's external feedback configuration ( 0x04 = 0x80 ) before calculating a setpoint or enabling VOUT, verify that configuration over I2C, and reject setpoints outside 800–12000 mV rather than clamping silently. If VOUT is already enabled in the wrong feedback mode, it shall be disabled before correction. The range remains subject to bench calibration (Assumption A-4 ). SRS-PWR-014 Firmware shall confirm the applied VOUT setpoint by reading back the PAC1934 VOUT channel within a bounded settling time and flag a setpoint-mismatch condition if the measured value does not converge. SRS-PWR-015 Revised 2026-10-15 (added the MANUAL exception to the ERROR clause). Firmware shall not enable VOUT or the transducer branch in ERROR — unless a manual request has since been made, in which case MANUAL shall take priority and enabling shall be allowed — while a fault is latched, or while the bootloader is active (Section 3). The latched-fault and bootloader clauses are not affected by a manual request.

After two consecutive samples at or above the limit, it shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off and enter ERROR. In every mode, each trip shall be logged as a WARNING event ( SRS-MON-032 ). SRS-PROT-022 In NORMAL mode, firmware shall monitor PAC1934 current readings on the VOUT and +5_TRANS channels against limits (default 1000 mA each, set with the limit command and stored in internal EEPROM). After three consecutive samples above a limit, it shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off and enter ERROR. In every mode, each trip shall be logged as a WARNING event ( SRS-MON-032 ). The check is independent of the eFuse's own hardware current limit. SRS-PROT-023 A latched fault shall remain latched until cleared by command: Modbus coil 00003 or the fault clear console command. The clear shall be refused while a fault input is still active. Firmware shall not auto-clear a latched fault. SRS-PROT-024 Because U2 (MCU branch) cannot be switched off by firmware, a fault on the MCU branch itself shall be reported but cannot be remediated by firmware power-cycling itself; only telemetry/fault reporting applies.
