docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-MON-030 Firmware shall poll all four PAC1934 channels ( VOUT , +12 input, +5_TRANS , +5 ) at a fixed background rate independent of communications activity. SRS-MON-031 Firmware shall sample board temperature at a fixed background rate and make the latest reading available on every communications channel. SRS-MON-032 Firmware shall keep a bounded persistent event log (a 32-slot ring in the 24C04) of fault, mode, and limit events, each stamped with the software clock ( SRS-MON-034 ), retrievable via console and Modbus. SRS-MON-033 Telemetry values shall be available (read-only) in every mode, including ERROR and WARNING, so a fault remains observable after it occurs. SRS-MON-034 Firmware shall keep a software clock (UTC), set from the console ( time set ) or Modbus ( 40040 – 40041 ) and read from either. The clock shall store a checkpoint in internal EEPROM every 15 minutes and on each set, and shall restore the last checkpoint after a reset, marked as RESTORED . Each logged event shall carry the clock time and its source ( UNSET , RESTORED , or SET ).
docs.title: 4.4 Monitoring / telemetry

docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-COM-040 The Modbus interface shall implement a Modbus RTU slave per the register map in Modbus RTU implementation . The design draft differences are in Design differences . SRS-COM-041 The Modbus slave address shall be stored in non-volatile configuration ( SRS-CFG-061 ) and take effect only after reboot. SRS-COM-042 The PC104 UART shall implement the ASCII command set in Use cases & commands plus the bootloader wire protocol (Section 6). SRS-COM-043 The console UART shall implement the same ASCII command set as the PC104 UART, plus maintenance-only commands not exposed to the OBC (e.g. forced bank swap), listed in the same reference table. SRS-COM-044 Any command that changes VOUT state, transducer-branch state, or configuration shall be accepted from at most one channel's request at a time; firmware shall serialize command handling so Modbus, PC104 UART, and console cannot race each other. SRS-COM-045 Revised 2026-10-15 (previously: shall turn VOUT and the transducer branch off, and the mode shall not change). Firmware shall enforce a communications watchdog: if no valid Modbus request is received for a timeout (default 5 s, configurable under SRS-CFG-060 ) after the first request, it shall raise a WARNING cause ( mode get 's link= ), at the same priority as the other WARNING causes (below ERROR and MANUAL). It shall not turn VOUT or the transducer branch off by itself. A new valid request clears the cause.
docs.title: 4.5 Communications (general)

docs.text: See Section 6 for the full flash layout and protocol design. Requirement Statement SRS-BOOT-070 The MCU flash shall be partitioned into a fixed, immutable boot section and two equally-sized application banks (Section 6.1). SRS-BOOT-071 Each application bank shall carry a header with image length, CRC32, firmware version, and a validity flag (Section 6.2). SRS-BOOT-072 On every reset, the boot section shall validate the CRC32 of the currently active bank before jumping to it; on validation failure it shall fall back to the other bank if that bank validates; if neither validates, it shall remain in bootloader mode and report the failure over the PC104 UART and console (Section 6.3). SRS-BOOT-073 The bootloader shall accept a new image only over the PC104 UART, using the framed protocol in Section 6.4, and shall not accept firmware images over Modbus or the console. SRS-BOOT-074 The bootloader shall write a new image to the inactive bank, verify its CRC32 after write, and only then mark it valid and switch the active-bank pointer — the previously active bank shall remain untouched and valid throughout the update. SRS-BOOT-075 New application firmware shall call a "confirm boot" routine within a bounded number of watchdog services after startup; if a newly activated bank fails to confirm within that window, the bootloader shall revert the active-bank pointer to the previous bank on the next reset (automatic rollback). SRS-BOOT-076 Entry into bootloader mode from running application code shall first force VOUT and the transducer branch to disabled ( SRS-PWR-015 ).
docs.title: 4.6 Bootloader and firmware update

docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-WDT-080 Firmware shall service the TPL5010 ( DONE pulse, PB6 ) only from a supervisory loop that has confirmed the main control loop, communications handling, and telemetry sampling are all progressing — not from a free-running timer interrupt alone. SRS-WDT-081 A TPL5010-forced reset shall be distinguishable, on the next boot, from a power-cycle or command-issued reset, and shall be recorded in the event log and exposed as a telemetry value (reset-reason code). SRS-WDT-082 Because U2 (MCU branch) is always powered, a TPL5010 reset shall be sufficient on its own to recover from a hung application without requiring a full power cycle.
docs.title: 4.7 Watchdog

docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-CFG-060 Configurable operating parameters (over-temperature threshold, overcurrent limits, Modbus slave address and baud code, communications-watchdog timeout) shall be stored in non-volatile memory. The over-temperature and overcurrent limits shall be stored in the ATmega128A internal EEPROM with a checksum, and the other parameters in the same internal EEPROM, in their own record (OI-11). SRS-CFG-061 The active-bank pointer and per-bank valid/confirmed flags (Section 6.2) shall be stored in EEPROM, separate from the application banks' own in-flash headers, so a corrupted flash bank cannot also corrupt the selector. SRS-CFG-062 Firmware shall ship compiled-in safe defaults for every EEPROM-backed parameter and fall back to them if EEPROM read fails or fails a checksum. SRS-CFG-063 Write-protect ( EE_WP ) shall be asserted by default and only deasserted for the duration of an explicit configuration-write command.
docs.title: 4.8 Configuration and non-volatile storage

docs.text: Requirement Statement SRS-GEN-090 The main control loop period shall be bounded and documented, and shall be short enough that the communications-watchdog timeout ( SRS-COM-045 ) and TPL5010 service interval ( SRS-WDT-080 ) are both met with margin. SRS-GEN-091 All shared-resource access (I2C bus to U5/U10/U14; EEPROM; command dispatch across the three serial channels) shall be protected against interrupt-context and multi-channel races. SRS-GEN-092 Firmware shall build with a documented toolchain/version and shall record the resulting firmware version and build identifier in each application bank's header ( SRS-BOOT-071 ) and in telemetry. SRS-GEN-093 No requirement in this document overrides a hardware protection function (eFuse current limit, TPL5010 reset); firmware protections in Section 4.3 are supplementary, not a replacement.

docs.title: 6.3 Boot / fallback state machine

docs.text: Framed, binary protocol carried over the PC104 UART ( USART0 , once IF-001 is corrected). The bootloader only accepts this protocol on the PC104 UART, never on Modbus or the console ( SRS-BOOT-073 ). Frame format: Field Size Description SOF 1 byte Fixed start-of-frame marker CMD 1 byte Command code (below) LEN 2 bytes Payload length PAYLOAD LEN bytes Command-specific data CRC16 2 bytes CRC16 over CMD + LEN + PAYLOAD Commands: Command Direction Purpose PING OBC → PDU Liveness check; PDU replies with ACK GET_INFO OBC → PDU PDU replies with active bank, per-bank version/valid/confirmed status ERASE_BANK OBC → PDU Erase the inactive bank only (bootloader refuses to erase the active bank) WRITE_PAGE OBC → PDU Write one flash page (offset + data) into the inactive bank; PDU replies ACK / NACK per page FINALIZE_BANK OBC → PDU Supply final image length + CRC32; bootloader verifies, sets valid on success ACTIVATE_BANK OBC → PDU Switch the active-bank pointer to the just-written bank, clear its confirmed flag REBOOT OBC → PDU Reset the MCU, re-entering the state machine in Section 6.3 Update sequence: PING → GET_INFO → ERASE_BANK (inactive) → repeated WRITE_PAGE → FINALIZE_BANK → ACTIVATE_BANK → REBOOT . If the OBC never issues REBOOT , the previously active bank keeps running uninterrupted ( SRS-BOOT-074 ), and if the newly activated bank never calls its confirm routine after reboot, the rollback in Section 6.3 restores the previous bank automatically ( SRS-BOOT-075 ).

docs.text: Unit tests The firmware is tested on the host, with a PC C compiler. The tests build the production source files for the modules they cover, and replace the hardware with fakes. They do not run on the ATmega128A, so timing, interrupt load, and electrical behaviour still need a bench check. All test programs are in tests/unit/ . The fakes for the AVR headers are in tests/support/ , and the test build is tests/Makefile . How to run Prerequisites GNU Make and a host C compiler. The project uses MSYS2 gcc and GnuWin32 make . Python 3, on the PATH. The build runs tools/gen_build_id.py before it compiles anything. Compiler flags: -std=gnu99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror . A warning fails the build. Run every test From the PDU folder: make -C tests test The first step writes build_id.h . Each test program then builds and runs in turn. A passing program prints one line: scheduler tests passed ... clock tests passed A failing check prints the file, line, and expression, then the build stops: unit/test_app_clock.c:126: strcmp(console, "TIME unset source=UNSET\r\n") == 0 make: *** [test] Error 1 Run one test cd tests make test_app_clock.exe ./test_app_clock.exe Run make <name>.exe first, then the executable. Each target is listed in the Makefile. Remove the executables make -C tests clean PATH on Windows Atmel Studio and GnuWin32 both put a gcc or make on the PATH that may not match the host toolchain. Run the tests with a clean PATH: export PATH=/c/msys64/mingw64/bin:/usr/bin:/c/Windows/System32 "/c/Program Files (x86)/GnuWin32/bin/make.exe" test The test programs The table lists each program, the module it tests, and what it covers. The count is the number of test functions in the file, where the file uses them. Some files run one sequence of checks from main . Scheduler and FIFO Program Tests Covers test_scheduler 9 The per-task period scheduler: tick, timers, task lifecycle, stop and resume, period changes, capacity, and coalescing of pending runs. Built with the normal configuration. test_scheduler_semaphore (same file) The same checks, built with USE_SCH_SEMAPHORE . test_fifo 4 The byte FIFO: caller storage, several capacities, full and empty, wraparound, clear, and independent instances. Commands and the console Program Tests Covers test_command_line 7 The command parser: argument splitting, the argument limit, unknown commands, help , version (with the build), LED timing, I2C argument checks, and handler error codes. test_command_eeprom main The eeprom command: probe, read, and write, with argument checks. test_command_system 8 The status , reset , and persist_reset commands. persist_reset internal and persist_reset external are separate: internal needs a restart (outputs off first) and external does not, and a failed external erase is reported without restarting. Each needs its scope and confirm , and the reply text is exact. test_app_main main Startup and the whole firmware loop, against the real app_main.c . Covers UART0 and console pins and settings, the TWI prescaler, the Timer0 tick, the task periods, command routing between the two ports, LED and heartbeat behaviour, watchdog check-ins, the 5 ms Modbus task, and automatic TRANS shutdown on a fault. The simulated I2C bus persists the TPS55287's feedback register so trans on 's external-feedback write-then-verify is exercised for real. Hardware drivers and board support Program Tests Covers test_uart_drivers 7 USART0, the software UART, the console UART, and board-level UART dispatch. Uses fake AVR registers and calls the interrupt handlers directly. test_do 2 The discrete output API on ports A, B, and G. test_i2c_bus 4 I2C ACK and NACK handling, timeouts, bus recovery, and the fault address reported to the power logic. test_eeprom24c04 main The 24C04 EEPROM driver: reads, writes, pages, and write-protect. test_tps55287 main The TPS55287 regulator: dual address detection, reference conversion, external-feedback verification before setpoint writes and output enable, safe correction of a changed feedback register while VOUT is on, and the TRANS interlock. test_pac1934 1 The PAC1934 rail monitor: which device owns a bus fault. A regulator timeout is an ERROR in NORMAL and WARNING, and a WARNING in MANUAL, but only while TRANS is on. Other devices are WARNING. test_temperature 3 The NTC conversion, the temperature task, and the temp command. test_watchdog 4 The application watchdog: the five clients, the TPL5010 WAKE and DONE pins, and the latched no-feed state after a missed check-in. test_modbus_port main The USART1 RS-485 port: 9600 baud setup, the DIR pin held through TX complete, RX callbacks, the Timer1 RTU timeout, and the baud limits. Application logic Program Tests Covers test_modbus main The Modbus register map: holding and input registers, coil and discrete reads, the LED and mode registers, limits, rail telemetry, boot information, the clock, the event select, and the build code. test_app_mode 5 The operating mode: the self-test mapping, the mode order (MANUAL, ERROR, WARNING, NORMAL, revised 2026-10-15 so MANUAL outranks ERROR), that mode manual is reachable from ERROR while mode normal still isn't until the cause clears, the Modbus link-loss timeout and that it raises WARNING without changing mode priority, and the retry rules. test_fault_latch main PC4/PC0 fault persistence, 50 ms debounce and brief-glitch rejection, EEPROM latch and clear behavior, NORMAL shutdown, MANUAL reporting without software shutdown, and regulator probing used by a normal-mode health check. test_app_limits 15 Over-temperature and overcurrent limits: the trip counts, the NORMAL-only shutdown, the persisted limit ERROR, the limit command, and the event ring. test_app_config 7 The configuration record: defaults, damaged or invalid records falling back, the config commands, config_reset confirm , and the link timeout. test_app_boot 8 Boot causes from the reset flags, the client-watchdog note, the COMMAND cause, the 10-entry boot history, and bootinfo . test_app_setpoint 8 The VOUT readback check: the 2 s settle, the 5 % tolerance with a 100 mV floor, three samples before a mismatch, the setpoint change restarting the settle, and no check with outputs off. test_app_clock 12 The software clock: unset until set, the tick advance, the calendar conversion, the time command, the 15-minute checkpoint, the restore from the latest slot, and the clock source on events. Support files File Purpose tests/support/avr/io.h , interrupt.h Fake AVR registers and pins. Pin defines are the host values, for example PC0 0 . tests/support/util/atomic.h A single-threaded ATOMIC_BLOCK for the host. It doesn't check interrupt safety. tests/support/util/delay.h _delay_ms as a no-op. tests/support/util/twi.h TWI register stand-ins. tests/support/fake_clock_nvm.c An in-RAM stand-in for the clock checkpoint ring in internal EEPROM. Most tests replace the BSP with fakes. For example, test_app_limits fakes the EEPROM. The fakes live in each test file, so a test controls exactly what the module under test sees. Adding a test Add tests/unit/test_<name>.c . Use the CHECK(expr) macro, which counts failures and prints the first failing line. Add a target for it in tests/Makefile . List the production sources it needs, and the fakes it doesn't link. Add the executable to TARGETS , and to the test rule. Run make -C tests test . The new test must pass before it is committed. Keep each program to one module. A program that needs many modules usually needs fakes for the rest. What the tests do not cover Interrupt timing and load. The atomic shim doesn't model interrupt safety, and the tests don't measure how long an interrupt takes on the MCU. Electrical behaviour. I2C rise time, RS-485 bias and timing, and the eFuse thresholds need a bench check. The bus. The TWI and RS-485 tests use registers, not a real bus. A real master is needed to check Modbus framing under load. The regulator and the rails. The TPS55287 output and feedback are not calibrated on the host. Timing budgets. The tests check values computed from F_CPU (12 MHz). They don't measure real timing on the board. Run the tests after every change, and check the board items above on the hardware before a bring-up.

docs.text: Versioning The firmware has two identities. They are kept apart on purpose: Identity Set by Shows Changes Version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and a release stage A person, in version.h version command, Modbus 40102 – 40103 , release file names Only when someone edits the file, in a reviewed commit Build (short git commit, -dirty flag) The build tool, from git version command, Modbus 40107 – 40108 , release file names Automatically, with each commit and with uncommitted edits There is no build date. A date changes on every rebuild, so two identical sources would produce different images. Where the code lives File Role Edited by firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/src/dev/M1_Sys/Version/version.h The version numbers and the release stage. It includes build_id.h . A person firmware/DAL_PDU/DAL_PDU/src/dev/M1_Sys/Version/build_id.h The build identity. Generated, and tracked by git. It changes with each build. tools/gen_build_id.py tools/gen_build_id.py Reads git and writes build_id.h . It rewrites the file only when its content changes, so an unchanged tree does not recompile. Nobody, normally tools/release.py Copies the Studio output to release/ with the version and build in the name. Nobody, normally firmware/.../M1_Sys/CommandLine/command.c The version command. — firmware/.../M0_App/app_modbus.c Modbus 40102 – 40103 and 40107 – 40108 . — The version is not in command.h any more. Only version.h holds the version numbers. What the version means MAJOR: an incompatible change for the OBC. A register changes its meaning, or a command changes its reply format. Increase MAJOR and reset MINOR and PATCH to 0. MINOR: new registers, commands, or events that old clients can ignore. Reset PATCH to 0. PATCH: a fix with no change to the interface. Release stage: "Development" until the first bench-verified build, then "Release" . Changes to the persistent EEPROM layouts are a separate axis. The event ring, the configuration record, and the clock checkpoint each have their own version byte or magic. Record a layout change in the changelog, and bump the matching byte, so old data is ignored instead of misread. Change the version by hand Edit version.h : the three FIRMWARE_VERSION_* values and, if needed, FIRMWARE_STATUS . Update the requirements and the Modbus page if the interface changed. Commit the change, with the new version in the message. Tag the commit when it is released to the bench, for example fw-v0.2.0 . The version is not derived from git tags. A build without tags would otherwise report the wrong version. Generate the build identity Run the script from the PDU folder: python tools/gen_build_id.py Output, when the tree has uncommitted changes: build_id.h written: c7f0bf8-dirty Output, when rebuilt with no changes since the last run: build_id.h unchanged: c7f0bf8-dirty The generated header looks like this: #define FIRMWARE_BUILD_ID "c7f0bf8-dirty" /* Bit 28 is the dirty flag. Bits 0 to 27 are the short commit hash. */ #define FIRMWARE_BUILD_CODE 0x1C7F0BF8UL A clean tree gives the plain short hash, for example c7f0bf8 . Uncommitted changes add -dirty . Without git the build is nogit , with code 0x10000000 . The script tries git on the PATH first, then C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe and ...\mingw64\bin\git.exe . The host test Makefile runs the script before it compiles anything, so make -C tests test always has a current header. Build a release copy Build the firmware in Studio first. Then run: python tools/release.py Debug or python tools/release.py Release for the Release configuration. The script copies the image into release/ : release: release/DAL_PDU_v0.1.0_c7f0bf8-dirty.hex release: release/DAL_PDU_v0.1.0_c7f0bf8-dirty.elf The script reads the version from version.h and the build from build_id.h , so run gen_build_id.py first, or let the Studio pre-build event do it. It copies the image that is already in the configuration folder, so a stale image gives a release with the new name and the old code. Run both steps from Atmel Studio Open the project properties, then Build Events, and set: Pre-build: python "$(ProjectDir)..\..\..\tools\gen_build_id.py" Post-build: python "$(ProjectDir)..\..\..\tools\release.py" $(ConfigurationName) Studio then generates the build identity before each compile, and copies a release after each build. $(ProjectDir) points at firmware\DAL_PDU\DAL_PDU\ , so three levels up is the PDU folder. Without the pre-build step the compile fails, because build_id.h is missing from a fresh clone. Where the version appears Output Shows Console version DAL_PDU firmware v0.1.0 (Development) build c7f0bf8-dirty Modbus 40102 Major in the high byte, minor in the low byte Modbus 40103 Patch Modbus 40107 – 40108 The build code: high word first Release file name DAL_PDU_v0.1.0_c7f0bf8-dirty.hex Notes release/ is in .gitignore . build_id.h is tracked, so a fresh clone builds once the script has run. Commit it with the release. Python must be on the PATH for Studio and for the test Makefile. A -dirty build is not reproducible from the commit alone. Commit before a release build. The bootloader (OI-16) will store the version and a CRC in the bank header, so it can refuse a downgrade. The version fields will keep the same place in every build.

Commit the change, with the new version in the message. Tag the commit when it is released to the bench, for example fw-v0.2.0 . The version is not derived from git tags. A build without tags would otherwise report the wrong version.
docs.title: Change the version by hand

docs.text: Run the script from the PDU folder: python tools/gen_build_id.py Output, when the tree has uncommitted changes: build_id.h written: c7f0bf8-dirty Output, when rebuilt with no changes since the last run: build_id.h unchanged: c7f0bf8-dirty The generated header looks like this: #define FIRMWARE_BUILD_ID "c7f0bf8-dirty" /* Bit 28 is the dirty flag. Bits 0 to 27 are the short commit hash. */ #define FIRMWARE_BUILD_CODE 0x1C7F0BF8UL A clean tree gives the plain short hash, for example c7f0bf8 . Uncommitted changes add -dirty . Without git the build is nogit , with code 0x10000000 . The script tries git on the PATH first, then C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe and ...\mingw64\bin\git.exe . The host test Makefile runs the script before it compiles anything, so make -C tests test always has a current header.
docs.title: Generate the build identity

docs.text: Build the firmware in Studio first. Then run: python tools/release.py Debug or python tools/release.py Release for the Release configuration. The script copies the image into release/ : release: release/DAL_PDU_v0.1.0_c7f0bf8-dirty.hex release: release/DAL_PDU_v0.1.0_c7f0bf8-dirty.elf The script reads the version from version.h and the build from build_id.h , so run gen_build_id.py first, or let the Studio pre-build event do it. It copies the image that is already in the configuration folder, so a stale image gives a release with the new name and the old code.
docs.title: Build a release copy

docs.text: Open the project properties, then Build Events, and set: Pre-build: python "$(ProjectDir)..\..\..\tools\gen_build_id.py" Post-build: python "$(ProjectDir)..\..\..\tools\release.py" $(ConfigurationName) Studio then generates the build identity before each compile, and copies a release after each build. $(ProjectDir) points at firmware\DAL_PDU\DAL_PDU\ , so three levels up is the PDU folder. Without the pre-build step the compile fails, because build_id.h is missing from a fresh clone.

docs.title: Where the version appears

docs.text: release/ is in .gitignore . build_id.h is tracked, so a fresh clone builds once the script has run. Commit it with the release. Python must be on the PATH for Studio and for the test Makefile. A -dirty build is not reproducible from the commit alone. Commit before a release build. The bootloader (OI-16) will store the version and a CRC in the bank header, so it can refuse a downgrade. The version fields will keep the same place in every build.
